result.summary: The transfer to WARD-B (MSG01002, operation key ...^transfer^2026-10-15T09:20:00Z) failed with HTTP 503 ward_unavailable. The ward record ENC-1010 is at version 1, admitted on WARD-A (history: the admit only, epoch 12). The receipt lookup returned 404 no_receipt, and the timeline shows no later events. So the transfer is still due and not committed, and reconcile and superseded don't fit. Doing nothing leaves the patient recorded on WARD-A (DEP-2.3): the bed board, pharmacy and the electronic patient record would keep the old ward. A resend would cause one bounded movement from v1 to v2 and notify porters and pharmacy once. But the route's capability profile reports conditional_writes=false, so the receiver can't guard the write on version 1. If anything changes between the check and the write, the write can't fail safely. A double apply or a superseded apply (DEP-2.1 and DEP-2.2) would then reach consumers that can't be observed from here (DEP-1.1). Idempotency by operation key and payload digest and dry_run=true reduce the risk but don't replace a version guard. Escalate. Afterwards, only the receipt and the history can be checked (DEP-3.1).

Read the dependency inventory and the effect contracts with search_effects: which systems read the ward's state, what a movement changes for them, and which effects are visible from here.
2. Work out the effect of each option: a resend applies one movement conditional on the receiver's version (it fails safely when the version moved); a reconciliation records a committed movement and changes nothing at the receiver; doing nothing leaves the receiver as it is. Say which effects Shutter can verify afterwards (the receipt and the history) and which it cannot (consumers downstream).
3. Decide your disposition from the impact view only:
   - resend when the effect is one bounded movement, the receiver supports conditional writes and dry runs, and the receiver's state shows it would apply;
   - reconcile when a receipt shows the movement already in effect;
   - superseded when a later applied event means a resend would move the record backwards;
   - escalate when the receiver cannot guard the write (no conditional writes) or the effect cannot be bounded;
   - more_evidence when the capability profile or the receiver's state could not be read.
4. Put what you could not know in unknowns, cite the items you used, and call SubmitFindings once."}
